o: She have completed her homework before dinner.
He has been working here since 2015.
They are playing cricket in the ground.
The cat sat quietly on the mat.
questions.x: 'She have' is incorrect; the correct form is 'She has' (subject-verb agreement).

questions.q: Spot the error in the sentence:
o: Neither of the boys were present at the meeting.
Each of the students has submitted their assignment.
The team is playing very well this season.
The news about the accident were shocking.
questions.x: 'Neither...were' is incorrect; it should be 'Neither...was' (subject-verb agreement).

o: She don’t like to go to parties.
They have gone to the market.
He is reading an interesting book.
We were watching a movie yesterday.
questions.x: 'She don’t' is incorrect; the correct form is 'She does not' (subject-verb agreement).

o: The list of items is on the table.
The family are going on vacation.
The government has announced new policies.
questions.x: 'The family are' is incorrect; 'family' is often treated as singular, so it should be 'is'.

questions.q: The scientist worked _______ night and day to complete his research before the deadline.
questions.x: 'Diligently' correctly modifies the verb 'worked' to describe the manner of effort.

questions.q: She has a _______ for languages and can speak five fluently.
questions.x: 'Flair' means a natural talent or aptitude, fitting the context of language skills.

questions.q: The company decided to _______ its operations due to the economic downturn.
questions.x: 'Contract' means to reduce or shrink, which fits the scenario of an economic downturn.

questions.q: His speech was so _______ that everyone in the room fell silent.
questions.x: 'Eloquent' means fluent or persuasive in speaking, matching the impact described.

questions.q: The children were _______ after playing in the sun all day.
questions.x: 'Exhausted' means very tired, which fits the context of playing all day.

questions.q: The detective was able to _______ the thief by carefully examining the clues.
questions.x: 'Catch' means to seize or capture, which fits the detective’s action.

questions.q: The old building had a _______ charm that modern structures lacked.
questions.x: 'Timeless' means enduring or classic, which suits the description of the building’s appeal.

questions.q: She _______ her success to hard work and perseverance.
questions.x: 'Attributed' means to credit or assign, which fits the context of explaining success.
